channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Canabidiol: amiga de Lulinha enviou a Marcola proposta de R$ 626 milhões
item.description: Businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger sent a contract draft to Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, aka Marcola, then chief of staff to President Lula, proposing a non‑bidding sale of up to R$ 626 million in cannabidiol‑based medicines to the Health Ministry. The draft was discovered on the phones of Roberta and Antonio Carlos Camilo Antunes, known as 'Careca do INSS', and indicates the scheme was facilitated by Lula’s son, Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha). Although the deal never materialized, the Federal Police are investigating the parties for alleged influence‑peddling and corruption.

item.title: Poder360 abre acesso ao Políticos do Brasil, com dados desde 1998
item.description: Poder360 launched 'Políticos do Brasil', a database with all candidates' info since 1998, including asset evolution and detailed profiles. Free access during 2026 election period; Poder Drive subscribers get full archive.

item.title: Poder360 abre acesso ao Agregador de Pesquisas mais completo da mídia
item.description: Poder360 opened free access to its Poll Aggregator for the 2026 elections, compiling over 620 surveys. The tool allows filtering by round, scope, moving average, and polling firm, showing voting intention trends with Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) highlighted as frontrunners in presidential polls.

item.title: Mesmo com apoio de Alcolumbre, avanço de prioridades de Lula é incerto antes das eleições
item.description: Despite Lula's rapprochement with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, priority government PECs (ending the 6×1 work scale and public security) will likely only advance in the Senate's CCJ after elections. Committee chair Otto Alencar requires debate before voting, delaying consideration until senators return from campaign trails.

item.title: Políticos do PL mostram ônibus enfileirados em ato pró-Lula
item.description: PL politicians, including councilwoman Nina Braga and state deputy Paulo Mansur, denounced the PT's mobilization of over 100 chartered buses to bring supporters to Lula's reelection campaign launch in São Bernardo do Campo. They claim the event was artificially filled and funded by the party, without providing evidence.

item.title: Prazo para pedir voto em trânsito termina hoje: veja como solicitar
item.description: The deadline to request voting in transit for the 2026 elections is August 20. Voters outside their electoral domicile can request a temporary change of polling place via the TSE's online portal or in person at electoral courts. The modality allows voting for president, governor, senator, and deputies if staying in the same state, or only for president if in a different state.

item.title: Deputado distrital e federal são as vagas mais concorridas de 2026
item.description: The 2026 elections show high competition for district and federal deputy seats, averaging 17.8 candidates per seat in the Federal District and 15 per seat in the Chamber of Deputies. The presidency has 13 candidates, including Pablo Marçal, who is ineligible. The lowest competition is for governor (7.3 per seat) and senator (5.9 per seat).

item.title: E as eleições, hein?
item.description: A Metrópoles poll shows 81.1% of 1,167 readers have already decided their vote for the two Senate seats. Noblat's blog features articles on Lula and national politics.

item.title: De pai para filho: quem são os ‘nepobabies’ candidatos em 2026
item.description: The article maps the prevalence of political dynasties in the 2026 elections, highlighting children of legislators and former presidents running for federal and state offices. Families such as Bolsonaro, Lira, and Calheiros illustrate how surnames, ally networks, and electoral strongholds are inherited, reinforcing the reproduction of oligarchies across the ideological spectrum.

item.title: Defesa de Lulinha avalia pedir queda total de sigilos de inquéritos ao STF
item.description: The defense of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, is considering requesting the Supreme Court to lift total secrecy on investigations against him in Justice André Mendonça's office. The move would be a strategic step to bring transparency to the proceedings.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro celebra com suspeitos de rachadinha em atos da campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) appeared at campaign events alongside two suspects accused of operating the 'rachadinha' kickback scheme in his former state deputy office. Their presence raises further questions about his ties to corruption.

item.title: Lula dobra menções à 'soberania' e esquerda encampa tema da Defesa
item.description: Lula's 2026 government program doubles mentions of 'sovereignty' (42 vs 22 in 2022) and emphasizes 'health' (43 mentions) and 'democracy' (19). The left adopts defense as a key theme.

item.title: A direita latino-americana está dividida em relação a Lula
item.description: The Latin American right is not unified in opposition to Lula. While Javier Milei adopts an openly hostile stance, other 'blue wave' presidents seek cordial and constructive relations with the Brazilian government.

item.title: Por que Flávio Bolsonaro ataca Lula, mas não muito, no caso Lulinha/Marcola
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has criticized Lula over the Lulinha/Marcola case, claiming that INSS corruption reached the president's office through Marcola. However, the Zero Um campaign has not pushed the investigations into Lula's son and former chief of staff to the forefront of its attacks, keeping the issue peripheral.

item.title: Marçal pode chegar ao primeiro turno sem saber se candidatura é válida
item.description: The Supreme Electoral Court is racing against time to rule on whether Pablo Marçal (PRTB) can run for president before the first round on October 4, despite his eight-year ineligibility. Rapporteur Minister Estela Aranha must receive registration requests by August 31, followed by a six‑day analysis period and possible defense stages that could stretch the decision close to election day.

item.title: Campanhas tentam evitar que Pablo Marçal vá aos debates
item.description: Campaigns pressure Band to exclude Pablo Marçal from the first 2026 presidential debate, arguing his party skipped rule-setting meetings and he is ineligible until 2032. The debate will likely feature only Renan Santos, Romeu Zema, and Ronaldo Caiado, with Lula absent and Flávio Bolsonaro attending only if Lula participates.

item.title: Charge do Aroeira
item.description: Aroeira cartoon and Noblat Blog articles cover investigations involving Lula's son, with Federal Police contradicting Minister Moraes in a Maranhão blogger case. Analyses discuss Lula's 2026 electoral prospects and current political scenario.

item.title: Tarcísio estuda nova forma de desgastar Haddad com taxa das blusinhas
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, running for re-election, is exploring strategies to undermine Fernando Haddad by linking him to the 'tax on blusinhas,' which was implemented during Haddad's tenure at the Finance Ministry. Lula advocates for the tax's repeal and blames Haddad for its creation, while Tarcísio criticizes the electoral timing of the measure.

item.title: A 45 dias do primeiro turno, Lula e Flávio evitam debates e sabatinas
item.description: With 45 days until the first round, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are avoiding debates and media interviews to minimize risks and attacks from opponents. While Lula's campaign questions candidate invitations and avoids being targeted alone, Flávio has stated he will only attend debates if Lula is present.

item.title: Confira agenda dos candidatos ao governo de SP nesta quinta (20/8)
item.description: The candidates for São Paulo governor continue their campaign agendas on the fifth official campaign day, with highlights for the main contenders Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and Fernando Haddad (PT). Haddad has a Record interview and walk in Capão Redondo, while Carlos Machado (PCB) launches government plan. Polls show Tarcísio leading with 50% of voter intentions.

item.title: Como atuava a consultoria de amiga de Lulinha que intermediava negócios em Brasília
item.description: The Federal Police is investigating businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of Lulinha, for mediating businesses in Brasília through RL Consultoria. Seized messages reveal contacts with companies holding federal contracts and attempts to close deals, including cannabis-based medications with a waiver of bidding at the Ministry of Health.

item.title: SP lidera mapa nacional de roubos de celular com 3 em cada 10 registros
item.description: São Paulo leads Brazil's ranking for cell phone thefts and robberies, accounting for 29% of devices registered in the National Restricted Cell Phone Database (BNCR). The database, with about 3 million records, was crucial for Operation Last Call, which recovered thousands of devices and notified suspects. The program integrates security forces to combat crime and the resale chain.

item.title: O cerco a Lula através do filho: oitivas enroladas e freio no Master
item.description: The Noblat panel discussed how the opposition could exploit investigations against Lulinha and Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola) to damage Lula's campaign. Lulinha's defense offered testimony multiple times, but the Federal Police and the Supreme Court rapporteur have not scheduled the hearing, extending the issue into the campaign. Attention was drawn to the silence surrounding the Banco Master scandal, involving Flávio Bolsonaro and calls with banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Como os números dos candidatos vão parar na urna? Entenda quem define e como funciona a escolha
item.description: Candidate numbers on electronic voting machines are defined by Brazil's Superior Electoral Court following specific rules for each position, with numbers typically drawn in party conventions. Candidates who already have a number associated with their name may keep it when running for the same office under the same party, which helps voters remember them.

item.title: Às vésperas da eleição, governo Lula avalia reduzir juros do Minha Casa, Minha Vida
item.description: The Lula government is considering lowering interest rates for Faixa 3 of the Minha Casa, Minha Vida program to benefit lower-income families. The measure is seen as an alternative to pressure from the construction sector to expand the program to the middle class.

item.title: Veja a agenda dos candidatos à Presidência nesta quinta-feira (20/8)
item.description: Thirteen presidential candidates have campaign schedules released for Thursday (8/20), with commitments across various regions of Brazil. Activities include technical visits, supporter meetings, live streams, and rallies, subject to change throughout the day.

item.title: Carlos Bolsonaro vira alvo de Amin por ser 'forasteiro' em SC e aposta em apoio de Jorginho Mello para eleição ao Senado
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro (PL) faces criticism for running for Senate in SC, being labeled an 'outsider' by Senator Esperidião Amin (PP), who uses the slogan 'true Catarinense'. Carlos relies on Governor Jorginho Mello (PL) for public defense, rejects opportunism accusations, and describes himself as a 'Catarinense by adoption'.

item.title: Com qual candidato a presidente você mais se identifica? Faça o teste do GLOBO e descubra
item.description: O GLOBO launched an interactive test with 14 questions for voters to discover which of the six main presidential candidates in 2026 they most identify with. The test covers topics such as the criminal age of majority, privatization of Correios, and ending the 6x1 work schedule, and includes direct responses from four candidates, while data on Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro were derived from public statements.

item.title: Palestino bolsonarista, prefeito costarriquenho, ator argentino, professor togolês: conheça os estrangeiros candidatos
item.description: The 2026 elections will feature at least 36 naturalized foreign-born candidates, including a Bolsonarista Palestinian, a Costa Rican mayor, an Argentine actor, and a Togolese professor. Since 2014, 156 foreign-born individuals have run for office in Brazil, with Portugal being the most common birthplace (21 candidates). Most candidates seek state or district-level legislative seats.

item.title: Da proibição total aos 'impostos altíssimos': veja o que os presidenciáveis defendem sobre as bets
item.description: The main 2026 presidential candidates adopt similar and restrictive postures toward online betting (bets), with measures ranging from total prohibition to higher taxes. Candidates like Lula and Tarcísio defend banning the practice, citing negative social and economic impacts, while the recently regulated sector faces new advertising rules and site suspensions by the government.

item.title: Onda de candidaturas de militares e policiais perde força em 2026 e retorna a patamar de 20 anos atrás
item.description: The number of candidacies by military and police personnel in the 2026 Brazilian elections fell by 35% compared to 2022, returning to the level of 950 candidates, last recorded in 2006. The reduction of 514 candidates breaks a growth trend observed since 2010, although military police remain the most numerous category.

item.title: Gravações temáticas e avaliação por grupo de eleitores: os bastidores das gravações de Lula para a campanha
item.description: President Lula has begun thematic recordings for his electoral propaganda, focusing on themes such as employment, sovereignty, health, and education to build an image library until the end of the first round. The campaign's communications team is evaluating whether to use spontaneous speeches or teleprompter-assisted delivery, testing both approaches in qualitative research to tailor the message to the public.

item.title: Inelegível, Marçal foca ataques em Lula e Renan Santos, e adversários veem jogo para favorecer Flávio
item.description: Pablo Marçal, registered as a presidential candidate despite being ineligible, is focusing his initial campaign attacks on fellow candidate Renan Santos and President Lula. Opponents see this as a strategy to indirectly benefit Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, whom Marçal has spared from criticism. The former coach is leveraging podcasts and social media to disseminate his critiques, gaining prominence and followers.

item.title: Flávio vai vincular caso Lulinha ao Planalto e abordar situação econômica das famílias em propaganda na TV
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) recorded electoral advertisements in a supermarket to address families' economic situation and plans to include the Lulinha case (Lula's son) in his campaign, linking it to influence-peddling investigations. The strategy combines attacks on the economy and corruption, using PF revelations about alleged ties between Lulinha, a businesswoman, and government aides.

item.title: Lobista que enviou minuta a ex-chefe de gabinete de Lula tentava acertar venda de R$ 626 milhões ao governo
item.description: Lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger sent a contract draft to Lula's former chief of staff, Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, for a R$ 626 million sale of cannabidiol medicines to the Health Ministry without bidding. Documents reveal a business plan for 1.2 million bottles of 36 drug types, also involving lobbyist Antonio Carlos Camilo Antunes.

item.title: Inquérito sobre pistoleiros no Maranhão atinge entornos de Flávio Dino e Carlos Brandão em meio à campanha eleitoral
item.description: A 2022 murder investigation in Maranhão exposes a R$ 778k kickback scheme in the Education Secretariat, implicating allies of Flávio Dino and Carlos Brandão. Gubernatorial candidate Felipe Camarão (PT) and Brandão's nephew are involved in the profit-sharing dispute. The case is now under Dino's rapporteurship at the STF, raising conflict of interest concerns.

item.title: Veja fotos da mansão usada por Lulinha e amiga lobista em Brasília
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger used a mansion in Brasília's Lago Sul for meetings, according to a former employee. The property, rented since 2024, was described as a meeting space rather than a permanent residence. Both are under investigation by the Federal Police for suspected influence peddling.

item.title: Chefe da Agência Antidrogas dos EUA diz que Argentina é 'modelo' para a região
item.description: DEA chief Terrance Cole praised Argentina's anti-drug strategy as a 'model for the region' during the 40th International Drug Enforcement Conference in Buenos Aires. The event, co-organized by Milei's government and the DEA, brings together over 100 countries to strengthen cooperation against transnational organized crime.

item.title: Prazo para pedir voto em trânsito termina nesta quinta (20/8)
item.description: The deadline to request absentee voting for the 2026 elections ends this Thursday (8/20). The procedure allows voters to cast ballots in another municipality if they won't be in their electoral zone on election day, with different rules for those within the same state versus another state. Requests can be made online via the TSE's Electoral Self-Service portal or in person at electoral courts.

item.title: Marcelo Aro coleciona inimigos e vira "candidato solo" em Minas
item.description: Marcelo Aro (PP) became a "solo candidate" for Senate in Minas Gerais after successive political ruptures. Former ally of Romeu Zema and Mateus Simões, he was labeled "bird of prey" and "traitor" when pursuing a gubernatorial bid with PL and Republicanos backing. The realignment with Cleitinho cooled, and his running mate Luiz Eduardo Falcão denied formal support, leaving Aro isolated in the race against Carlos Viana (PSD) and Superman (Novo).

item.title: Marcola pode atrapalhar mais Lula que Lulinha, avaliam pesquisas do PT
item.description: Internal PT polls show allegations against Marco Aurélio Santana (Marcola), Lula's former chief of staff, may damage the president more than those against his son Lulinha. Marcola's close proximity to Lula is seen as a greater risk factor, while Lulinha is viewed as an "old character" whose past controversies didn't gain traction. Both are under Federal Police investigation for links to lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger.

item.title: Em encontro no Alvorada, Lula volta a dizer que Lulinha deve se explicar
item.description: At a meeting in the Alvorada Palace, Lula reiterated that his son Lulinha must provide explanations to the Federal Police, without interference or special treatment. The meeting, focused on the São Paulo campaign, included lawyer Marco Aurélio de Carvalho, who advocated equal treatment for Lulinha.

item.title: El asesor Fernando Cerimedo y el poder en las sombras de la nueva derecha latinoamericana
item.description: The article exposes the transnational role of political consultant Fernando Cerimedo, a key figure in Latin America's new right. He ran troll farms and dirty campaigns for Milei in Argentina, advised Bolsonaro in Brazil during the attempt to block Lula's inauguration, and is now detained in Bolivia for assaulting his former partner while advising President Rodrigo Paz. The case illustrates how digital operators cross borders and wield power without public office, backed by disinformation ecosystems like 'La Derecha Diario'.

item.title: Tebet diz que eleição de 2026 pode significar “fim da polarização”
item.description: Senate candidate Simone Tebet (PSB) states the 2026 election could end the polarization harming Brazil. She warns that a Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) victory over Lula (PT) would extend extremism for 8-12 years, threatening national sovereignty. Tebet calls this the most important election in recent history, criticizing the far-right's irrelevant and regressive agenda.

item.title: Tebet critica multa a Lula e diz que presidente vai recorrer ao TSE
item.description: Simone Tebet (PSB) criticized the R$15,000 fine imposed on Lula for early campaign propaganda, stating she saw no wrongdoing at the May 19 event. She expects Lula to appeal to the TSE and expressed confidence in a final acquittal.

item.title: Lobista “aparentemente” agia em nome de Lulinha, diz jornal
item.description: Federal Police investigate lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger for allegedly acting on behalf of Lulinha, President Lula's son, in negotiating a medicinal cannabis project with the Health Ministry. PF-obtained messages show she promised 20% commission on public contracts and cited ties to lawyer Otto Medeiros and Justice Kassio Nunes Marques. The case involves corruption and influence peddling suspicions, under Justice André Mendonça's rapporteurship at the Supreme Court.

item.title: Ciência e agricultura devem estar entre as prioridades
item.description: The article argues that, in the 2026 elections, science and innovation must be prioritized to ensure the sustainability of Brazil's agricultural production in the coming decades. It stresses the need to maintain research investments to support sustainable development in the sector.

item.title: Tarcísio participa nesta quinta da sabatina dos jornais O Globo e Valor Econômico e da Rádio CBN; acompanhe ao vivo
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas will be interviewed in a joint sabatina by CBN, O Globo and Valor Econômico on Thursday, following Fernando Haddad's appearance the day before. Tarcísio leads Haddad by 15 points in voting intentions, highlighting his administration's achievements such as the Sabesp privatization and infrastructure projects, while stressing women's issues as a central campaign theme.

item.title: Apesar de queda na fila no INSS, pessoas relatam espera de até 8 meses por resposta a pedido de benefício
item.description: Although the INSS benefits backlog fell to 1.55 million in July, many beneficiaries report waiting up to eight months for pension or aid responses, including app driver José Flávio and cook Erika Antônia. The government says the backlog has dropped 74% since the start of the year, while President Lula pledges to eliminate it by 2026.

item.title: Um terço dos candidatos afirma não ter bens a declarar ao TSE
item.description: About 33.6% of the 20,608 candidates registered for the 2026 elections declared having no assets to the TSE. Among the 13 presidential candidates, Hertz Dias (PSTU) and Rui Costa (PCO) reported no assets, as did vice-presidential candidate Raquel Brito (UP). The declaration is mandatory and self-reported, subject to verification.
